hints: You can find the largest value of nums in one pass. What extra thing would you need to remember during that same pass to also know the runner-up?
Keep two variables, first and second, for the largest and second largest distinct values. A new maximum pushes the old one down to second; a value strictly between them becomes the new second.

1. first = second = Long.MIN_VALUE (means 'not set').
  2. For each x: if x > first, then second = first, first = x.
  3. Else if x < first and x > second, second = x.
  4. Return -1 if second was never set, otherwise return it.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Sort the array, then scan from the end for the first value smaller than the maximum.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: One pass keeping the top two distinct values.

explain: For nums = [4, 9, 2, 9, 7]: 4 becomes first; 9 pushes 4 down to second; 2 changes nothing; the second 9 equals first and is ignored (we want distinct values); 7 is between 4 and 9, so second becomes 7 and the function returns 7. The x < first check is what handles duplicates of the maximum. If all values are equal, as in [5, 5, 5], second is never set and we return -1. Using a long sentinel means a real value of -109 is never confused with 'not set'.
recognize: "Second largest distinct value" → one pass tracking the top two.
javascript: function secondLargest(nums) { const s = [...new Set(nums)].sort((a, b) => b - a); return s.length > 1 ? s[1] : -1; }
